Your political career is already over.

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

Бросать трубку = to hang up. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw; to abandon', paired with 'бросить'.

examples.text: Он всегда бросает вещи на пол.
examples.trans: He always throws things on the floor.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

examples.trans: We'll upload the video to the internet.

examples.text: Ты зачем это видео в интернет выложила?
examples.trans: Why did you post that video on the internet?

Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'thief' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Plural only. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'боры'). Common substantive noun meaning 'election' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is running in the election.

examples.text: У меня много дел. Выборы мэра…
examples.trans: I've got a lot to do. The mayoral election...

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: The thing that ends is the subject. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to end, to be over', paired with 'заканчиваться'.
деньги закончились = the money ran out

examples.text: Всё, выборы закончились. Тебя начальник ждёт.
examples.trans: That's it, the election is over. Your boss is waiting for you.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: В интернете = on the internet. International borrowing from English 'Internet' ('inter-' + 'network').

examples.trans: Look it up on the internet.
Look it up on the internet.

meanings.note: A person's own room at work. From French 'cabinet' (private study or office).

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, я сейчас в кабинете у мэра.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, I'm in the mayor's office right now.

meanings.note: Staff or film frame. Common masculine noun meaning 'personnel, shot, frame' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: One must know how to work with personnel.
The cameraman captured an excellent shot.

examples.text: С кадрами нужно уметь правильно работать.
examples.trans: One must know how to work with staff properly.

meanings.note: Device for recording video. Common feminine noun meaning 'camera, video camera' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Of course, everything is recorded on camera.

examples.text: Нужно ходить по городу с камерой!
examples.trans: You need to walk around town with a camera!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'career' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты только что разрушил свою карьеру.
examples.trans: You have just destroyed your own career.
Your political career is already over.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'someone, somebody' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: to pursue and seize someone or something

examples.trans: There is nothing left to gain here, Pasha.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'over, above; at' in everyday speech.
смеяться над = to laugh at; form надо before мной

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ dative + infinitive: мне терять нечего = I have nothing to lose

examples.trans: There is nothing to do here.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, что я хочу. Мне терять нечего.
examples.trans: You know what I want. I have nothing to lose.

meanings.note: Plural, also the TV news programme. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'piece of news' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Core Russian num meaning 'one' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Её, ей, ей, о ней. Core Russian pron meaning 'she; it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to publish'.

examples.text: Кто-то опубликовал секретное видео в интернете!
examples.trans: Someone published a secret video on the internet!

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Answer to thanks. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ймать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to catch', paired with 'ловить'.

examples.text: Ты бандитов поймал! Которые банкомат на Гарибальди ограбили.
examples.trans: You caught bandits! Who robbed the ATM on Garibaldi Street.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'литический'). Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('political').

examples.trans: Your political career is already over.

meanings.note: Поставить защёлку = fit a latch. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to place (upright)', paired with 'ставить'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to place (upright)', paired with 'ставить'.

examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екретный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('secret').

examples.text: А почему он на секретном совещании?
examples.trans: And why is he at a secret meeting?

meanings.note: Not openly visible or disclosed. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'крытый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hidden, concealed, covert').

examples.text: В кабинете была установлена скрытая камера.
examples.trans: A hidden camera was installed in the office.

examples.text: В кабинете мэра была скрытая камера.
examples.trans: In the mayor's office there was a hidden camera.

meanings.note: смеяться над кем = to laugh at someone; perfective засмеяться = to start laughing

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'меяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to laugh', paired with 'засмеяться'.

examples.trans: Don't laugh. Read me the number.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

собирать.gloss: to collect, to gather, to pack

meanings.note: Money, signatures, or documents. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to collect, to gather, to pack', paired with 'собрать'.
собирать вещи = to pack one's things

examples.text: И мы начинаем готовить документы. Собирайте деньги!
examples.trans: And we're starting to prepare the documents. Gather the money!

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

Pack or assemble. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').
Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Directional adverb. Core Russian adv meaning 'there, thither' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: They put bad meat in there for you.

examples.text: Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: Want them to take you there too right now?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Уходи! = Go away!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.
+ infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Я что-то вижу = I see something. Core Russian pron meaning 'something; somehow' in everyday speech.
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
